answer: An agent economy can cap sybil clusters with a graph cut rule: trust flows from established agents through endorsement links, and a new identity gains weight only up to the capacity of the smallest vertex set separating it from that trusted core. A thousand fakes behind one gateway vertex share that gateway's tiny capacity, however they polish each other like crystal facets. One honest agent builds independent paths and gains full weight, while a farmer must buy many separate paths, each costing relationships and time, and the umber-dark cluster behind a single cut stays small.
